title.narrative: Empowering Women and Youth Smallholder Farmers in Groundnut Market System Development in the FCT.

description.narrative: There are about 38 million smallholder farmers in Nigeria (20% of the country’s population). 70% of Nigeria smallholder farmers are women, while the rest of the 30% are males. Despite their importance for the domestic economy and due to the sector’s productivity limitations, more than 72 percent of Nigeria’s smallholder farmers live below the poverty line of 3,050 Naira (USD 1.9) a day. The project aims to empower 50 women and youth smallholder farmers in Abuja, Nigeria, through focused interventions in groundnut seed management. The project shall focus on providing access to improved groundnut seed varieties, offering training on modern and sustainable farming practices, and facilitating the adoption of efficient seed storage and processing techniques. Furthermore, the project seeks to improve and strengthen the capacity of 50 women and youth in groundnut farming, enabling them to increase productivity, improve income, and contribute to food security. With access to quality seeds and training in best practices, women and youth farmers are likely to see improved yields to support the livelihoods of women and youth farmers. Additionally, the project will constitute the formation of a community group of farmers (the target beneficiaries) and market linkages to boost profitable trading opportunities and economic resilience.
